fullDescription: A paper-ground catalogue landing page for a made object: a cut-out subject standing over a huge ghosted outline numeral, a fixed progress spine, a vertical rail label and inspect controls that swap the variant across every figure on the page at once. Headlines mix solid and outlined words, and everything reveals through blur rather than fading. Good for furniture, tools, instruments and any maker selling numbered editions.

structured.summary: A paper-ground catalogue page for a made object: a cut-out subject standing over a ghosted outline numeral, a fixed progress spine down the top of the window, a vertical rail label, and inspect controls that swap the variant. Everything reveals through blur rather than fading.

style.description: Warm paper ground with near-black ink and one vermilion used only for markers, active states and the progress spine. The display face mixes SOLID and OUTLINED words in the same headline, which is the whole typographic idea. All small type is monospaced.
style.prompt: Apply a paper-catalogue style. Palette: ground #E8E6DF, secondary ground #DEDBD2, ink #151515, secondary ink #494844, muted #75736C, one vermilion #C4442C, hairlines rgba(21,21,21,.16). Typography: 'Familjen Grotesk' 500-700 uppercase for headings at letter-spacing -.03em to -.035em; 'Spline Sans Mono' 400-600 at 9.5-11.5px with letter-spacing .12em-.14em for labels and body. Border-radius 0 everywhere including buttons. MUST set at least one word of each major headline as an OUTLINE using color:transparent with -webkit-text-stroke, against solid words in the same line. MUST keep the vermilion to markers, active states and the spine, never a filled area. DO NOT use a gradient, a glow, a bento grid, rounded cards or a drop shadow anywhere.

layout_and_structure.description: A fixed left rail and progress spine frame six sections: a catalogue hero, a two-column detail, an editions table, a three-cell data grid, a process list and a close whose wordmark is cropped by the page edge.

prompts.prompt: A 2px progress spine pinned across the very top of the window, filling in the accent as the page scrolls. A 34px vertical rail down the left edge holding one line of rotated monospaced text with writing-mode: vertical-rl. Offset the page content by the rail width, and drop both on narrow screens.

Full viewport minus the nav on the secondary ground, overflow clipped. Behind everything, a huge outlined numeral at clamp(220px,44vw,660px) in transparent fill with a 1px stroke at low alpha. Left, a copy column no wider than 44vw: a monospaced eyebrow, a headline at clamp(38px,6.4vw,104px) mixing a solid first line with an outlined second, a monospaced lede and two square buttons. Right, the cut-out subject sized by HEIGHT. A bottom rail carries a monospaced instruction on the left, a hairline, and a counter on the right.

A vertical stack of small monospaced buttons pinned to the right edge at mid height, one per variant, using aria-pressed for state. On narrow screens they become a horizontal wrapping row below the subject.

A monospaced index tag with a hairline rule, an uppercase headline mixing solid and outlined words, a monospaced lede, and either hairline-ruled rows (accent label, description, right-aligned value) or a three-cell grid separated by 1px gaps over a hairline background.

Monospaced uppercase headers over a hairline, a display-face uppercase first column and monospaced metadata columns, each row hairline separated. Collapses to a two-column grid per row on narrow screens.

A headline mixing solid and outlined words, a monospaced fine-print line, two buttons at the opposite edge, a hairline footer strip, then the wordmark full width at clamp(70px,19vw,290px) translated down .17em so the page edge crops it.

special_ui_components.description: The reference reveals with a filter, not with a fade, and the difference is visible.
special_ui_components.prompt: Reveal elements from {opacity:0, translateY(26px), filter:blur(9px)} to their resting state over about .8s, staggering siblings by roughly .09s. The blur component is what makes this read as focus pulling in rather than as a plain fade. Reveal the hero subject from a heavier blur(14px) with no translate. Scope every start state to a class the script adds only when prefers-reduced-motion is not set, so the reduced-motion and no-JS renders are the finished page.

special_ui_components.description: The structural signature: a page-level indicator rather than a decorative bar.
special_ui_components.prompt: Pin a 2px element across the top of the viewport at a high z-index and set its width from scroll position over (scrollHeight - innerHeight). It is bound to position, so it runs backwards as the reader scrolls up, which is what stops the page feeling dead in reverse.

special_ui_components.description: A variant switcher where every figure on the page agrees.
special_ui_components.prompt: Put a huge outlined numeral behind the subject and let it counter-travel horizontally on scroll while the subject lifts and recedes. Wire the inspect buttons so that choosing a variant updates ALL of it at once: the subject's tint via a CSS filter, the ghost numeral, the counter in the bottom rail, the eyebrow, and the subject's aria-label. A page that says edition 04 in the counter and edition 01 in the eyebrow is broken, and it is the kind of break nothing warns you about. Store the chosen tint on the element so the scroll handler can re-apply it alongside its own blur instead of overwriting it.

special_ui_components.description: How to place a keyed subject so it survives every viewport.
special_ui_components.prompt: Size the subject by HEIGHT with width auto and a max-width, never by width plus an aspect-ratio: a width-driven box outgrows the hero on a short viewport, crops the object and buries the copy. On narrow screens move it into normal flow BELOW the copy at full width rather than leaving it behind the text. Verify its box sits inside the hero at several sizes. If the subject has real see-through gaps, such as the space between chair legs, do NOT fill holes when keying it, and despill toward the neutral mean rather than toward max(R,B) or a warm subject keeps a green cast that no single-channel test will catch.
Only the maker's own process and measurable facts. DO NOT invent press coverage, awards, stockist logos or review counts. Every figure that appears twice must agree.
